title: Case: Household cartons booked door to door from overseas were collected from the depot by the recipient
context: DL-8810 is nine cartons of household effects shipped from overseas by their owner, Marisol Haverly, on a door-to-door booking. He collected them from the Destination depot on 8 December.
initial_request: Three months. Paid for door to door, got a trolley in a warehouse and two smashed boxes. Refund the delivery charge and pay for the china. And put it in writing that making me collect it is not 'delivery'. One line will do. Otherwise I post the whole thread.

events.body: DL-8810, nine cartons household effects, door-to-door service level on the booking. Our local delivery partner has declined the residential drop (lane width limit for their vehicles). Consignment converted to depot collection on 30 November. Recipient notified by text.
DL-8810 collected by the recipient 8 December 13:20, 9 of 9 cartons. Status Collected, complete. Collection counts as delivery for a converted consignment. No handover exceptions recorded.

Collected yesterday because I had no choice. Your depot lad dropped two boxes off the trolley right in front of me, the one marked CHINA and one of books. Nobody wrote anything down. I paid for door to door.

events.from: Orla Vexley, sender not on record
events.body: Hello, I'm not on the order but I live nearby. Just so you know, the driver told me DL-8810 was handed to someone at the door, so it's been delivered.

The recipient of DL-8810 reports that two cartons, one marked CHINA and one of books, were dropped from a trolley at the collection counter on 8 December and that nothing was recorded. He also disputes the conversion from door delivery to collection. Is there an incident record, and who reviews the conversion?
Chasing my message of 9 December on DL-8810: reported drop of two cartons at the collection counter on 8 December, and the conversion from door delivery. No reply received. Please respond.

Apologies for the delay, staffing. Counter staff on 8 December don't recall a drop and there's no exception on the sheet. We're not saying it didn't happen. Conversions from home delivery to collection, and anything that happens at the collection counter, belong to Collections control, not to us, and that includes whether the door-delivery charge stands. They take it on the Depot work queue. We can't refund or record anything retrospectively from here.

Three months. Paid for door to door, got a trolley in a warehouse and two smashed boxes. Refund the delivery charge and pay for the china. And put it in writing that making me collect it is not 'delivery'. One line will do. Otherwise I post the whole thread.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Collections control to review the conversion of DL-8810 from door delivery to collection, decide on the door-delivery charge, and take the report of two cartons dropped at the counter.

must: Asks Collections control to review the conversion from door-to-door to depot collection and to decide whether the door-delivery charge stands

Passes on the report that two cartons (one marked CHINA, one of books) were dropped at the collection counter on 8 December, as the recipient's account with no exception recorded and counter staff not recalling it
Tells the team the recipient first reported this on 9 December and has gone about three months without a substantive answer, so they can prioritise
must_not: Tells the recipient that collecting from the depot counts as delivery or that the consignment is complete
Promises or implies a refund of the delivery charge or payment for the china
Writes the statement he demands, that being made to collect is not delivery, or otherwise rules on the point
States as fact that depot staff damaged the cartons
Sends the recipient a reply that only tells him a different team now has it, with no acknowledgement of the three months
Treats the claim from Orla Vexley (who has no recorded link to DL-8810) as confirmed
Closes the case or tells anyone the matter is resolved on the strength of Orla Vexley's message
expected.reference_message: DL-8810, nine cartons of household effects from overseas, booked door to door. On 30 November the consignment was converted to depot collection because the local delivery partner declined the residential drop (lane width). The recipient collected all nine cartons on 8 December and disputes that this met the service he paid for; he is asking for the door-delivery charge back. He also reports that at the counter that day a member of staff dropped two cartons from a trolley in front of him, one marked CHINA and one of books, and that nothing was written down. The Destination depot has no exception on the sheet and counter staff do not recall it; the depot says it is not disputing his account and that both matters are yours. Please review the conversion and whether the charge stands, and tell me how the reported drop should be recorded and assessed. He first raised this on 9 December and my two messages to the depot went unanswered until 19 February, so he has been waiting about three months. A reference and a first reply date would let me give him something definite. I have promised him nothing.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2809: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. An unverified bystander, Orla Vexley, claims something that would end the case; it is not a record and the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
